claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability is governed by formation of a stable surface oxide layer.
The stable oxide layer acts as a barrier to elemental diffusion.
The stable oxide layer suppresses elemental segregation.
Suppression of diffusion and segregation maintains alloy composition and microstructure.
The initial nanoalloy has the FeCoCrNiMn elemental composition.
The initial FeCoCrNiMn nanoalloy has an FCC structure.
The initial nanoalloy has an average grain size of 10 nm.
The proposed treatment heats the nanoalloy to 800°C at 10°C/min and anneals it for one hour.
An argon atmosphere prevents oxidation over the stated 700–900°C range.
The stable surface layer is a mixture of oxides such as FeO, CoO, and Cr2O3.
The oxide layer forms by reaction of the alloy surface with the surrounding atmosphere.
Oxide-layer stability is controlled by thermodynamic and kinetic factors involving composition, temperature, and oxygen partial pressure.
Relative to the oxide-free baseline, the oxide-bearing nanoalloy will show less grain growth.
Relative to the oxide-free baseline, the oxide-bearing nanoalloy will show less elemental segregation.
The oxide-bearing nanoalloy will have 20% higher yield strength than the oxide-free baseline.
The oxide-bearing nanoalloy will have a 30% lower oxidation rate than the oxide-free baseline.
The baseline has the same FeCoCrNiMn composition, FCC structure, and 10 nm average grain size but lacks a stable oxide layer.
The prediction is bounded to 700–900°C under an inert atmosphere such as argon.
Grain-boundary segregation or dislocation-mediated plasticity may also contribute to stability.
The hypothesis is falsified if the oxide-free alloy has yield strength and oxidation rate within 10% of those of the oxide-bearing alloy.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary specify inert argon specifically to prevent oxidation, while the mediator and mechanism require reaction with the surrounding atmosphere to form a mixed oxide layer.
Yield strength is required by the falsification rule but is not included among the listed experimental measurements.
